newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey abolishes cotton export quota - deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Turkey abolishes cotton export quota - deputy PM.

text.p: Turkey abolished an outstanding quota of 100,000 tonnes on cotton exports, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said on Tuesday.

"Our good news to cotton producers is that all levies and quotas (on cotton exports) have been abolished. They will have no problem in establishing their own prices or in exporting," Ciller told in news conference on economic issues.
Ciller said the change would take immediate effect.
A 100,000-tonne quota imposed on cotton exports during the 1995/96 season had remained in effect even though a 20 cent/kg a customs levy on cotton exports had been removed in December 1995.

Turkey forecasts cotton output at about 783,735 tonnes in 1996/97, down from 837,114 in 1995/96. But output is likely to be above the level that has been forecast due to expectations of a 17-year high outturn of 308,292 tonnes in the leading western Aegean region, against an initial prediction of 299,157.
